core.title: Seed acceptance given blocks with the canonical defaults
core.given: An acceptance criterion's given section is being authored or edited.
core.when: You fill in the given block (auth, builders, time, stubbing, knobs).
core.then: Start the given section from the canonical defaults: auth scopes [], builders [], time {}, stubbing policy strict with overrides [], knobs {}.
prefer: Add non-default values only where the acceptance's behaviour actually needs them.
Express any needed stub as an explicit entry in stubbing.overrides on top of the strict default.
When a harness template applies, let its given specialize these defaults instead of replacing them.
avoid: Granting auth scopes, adding builders, freezing time or setting knobs that the acceptance's behaviour does not require.
Relaxing the default strict stubbing policy merely to make an acceptance easier to satisfy.
core.why: A shared, minimal default given makes every criterion start from the same strict, permission-free baseline, so any extra setup is a deliberate, reviewable deviation.
evidence: Where a given field is not set by the acceptance, its effective value equals the canonical default (auth.scopes [], builders [], time {}, stubbing.policy strict, stubbing.overrides [], knobs {}).
Reviewer confirms each non-default given value is motivated by the acceptance's behaviour.
verification: A check confirms that wherever a given field is not set by the acceptance, its effective value equals the canonical default (auth.scopes [], builders [], time {}, stubbing.policy strict, stubbing.overrides [], knobs {}); it checks effective values and does not require every field to be serialized explicitly, nor does it forbid non-default values.
strict is the DEFAULT stubbing policy, applied only when none is specified; the check does not by itself reject an explicitly set non-default policy.

Detecting that an acceptance given section was added or edited requires a diff-level observer (needs_new_observer); the task-term signal (acceptance, criteria, given) is supporting only and does not gate activation.

values: acceptance given section added or edited

fires: Anyone (planner, coder or tooling) authors a new acceptance criterion and writes its given section.
An existing acceptance given section is edited, e.g. auth, builders, time, stubbing or knobs are added, changed or removed.
An acceptance given section is written outside a formal planning phase or without a task that declares acceptance.
doesNotFire: Only the when/then parts of an acceptance are edited and its given section is untouched.
Documentation or other non-acceptance prose is edited and contains no acceptance given section.

bunOnly.text: Term given_defaults ('the default given block.') values: auth: {scopes: []}; builders: []; time: {}; stubbing: {policy: strict, overrides: []}; knobs: {}.
bunOnly.reason: The term id given_defaults is a term-registry identifier of this rule in the ATDD-Bun realization; the core's verification names the defaults check generically. The values themselves are the stack-neutral canonical defaults, kept in core.then and core.verification.

classification.note: Already neutral: an acceptance-authoring situation with no stack, path or role terms.
The field list (auth, builders, time, stubbing, knobs) is the ATDD acceptance given-format vocabulary, not stack machinery; kept verbatim.
The single obligation. The canonical default values come from the ATDD criteria convention itself, so they stay in the core rather than a profile key.
stubbing.overrides is a given-format field of the acceptance criteria, neutral; not a stack API.
'Harness template' is the acceptance-test harness's template; role-level, no stack named.
Anti-pattern stated in given-format terms; neutral.
Anti-pattern stated in given-format terms; neutral.
Effective-value check; the core's verification describes the same check generically (effective defaults, not explicit serialization).
Human review of non-default values; advisory, not a machine check, so it stays as evidence only.
The canonical default values are core (mirrored in core.verification entry 1); the term id given_defaults is a realization identifier and is bunOnly.
Scope limit of the check: strict is the default policy only; an explicitly set non-default policy is not rejected by this rule alone. Mirrored in core.verification entry 2.
Diff-level change fact; its note (regardless of author role, phase or file location) is carried by the fires entries and the verification note on observers.
Supporting, non-gating task-term signal; values are methodology terms, not stack terms.

neutralityNotes: The whole convention is methodology-level: the given-block field vocabulary (auth, builders, time, stubbing, knobs) and the canonical default values come from the ATDD acceptance-criteria format carried in the legacy planner source, not from Bun or any runtime, so they remain in the core; a stack whose acceptance harness used a different field vocabulary would need that revisited, but no vocabulary key exists for it and none is proposed because it is part of the obligation itself, not stack structure. Activation is deliberately role-, phase- and location-agnostic, so no profile keys are required (profileRequirements is empty). Two neutralizations: 'wagon text' in doesNotFire (wagon is a stack layout concept, layout.wagon_dir) became 'other non-acceptance prose' with the operative gate 'contains no acceptance given section' unchanged; the term id given_defaults in verifier_detail[0] is classified bunOnly while its values stay core.
